evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voice_webhooks.rs:950 — verify_hmac_signature() reads VOICE_WEBHOOK_SECRET via `std::env::var(...).unwrap_or_else(|_| "default_secret".to_string())`, so when the env var is unset the HMAC key silently becomes the string literal `default_secret` (present in the open-source tree). Any attacker can compute a valid X-Webhook-Signature and forge Google Actions webhook requests — a fail-OPEN auth bypass.

This contradicts the repo's documented fail-CLOSED convention for every other webhook secret (backend/CLAUDE.md: PORTAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET 500 CONFIG_ERROR, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET 503 NOT_CONFIGURED, AIRBNB_WEBHOOK_SECRET 500 NOT_CONFIGURED when unset).

Reachability: router mounted at backend/servers/api-server/src/lib.rs:340 (routes::voice_webhooks::voice_webhook_router()); verify_hmac_signature called on the google branch at voice_webhooks.rs:712. Fix: fail closed when VOICE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset (mirror portal/stripe pattern), never default the key.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voice_webhooks.rs:700-708 — the `alexa` branch of webhook verification sets `valid: !request.signature.is_empty()` with no cryptographic check whatsoever: any non-empty string is accepted as a valid Alexa signature. There is no HMAC/certificate verification (Alexa requires SignatureCertChainUrl + RSA-SHA1 validation).

This is an authentication bypass for the Alexa voice webhook path on a production-mounted router (lib.rs:340). An attacker can send arbitrary payloads with any dummy signature header and pass verification.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voice_webhooks.rs:959 — verify_hmac_signature returns `Ok(signature == expected)`, a non-constant-time byte/String comparison of the provided vs computed HMAC. This leaks timing information usable to forge a valid signature byte-by-byte.

Every sibling webhook verifier in the same segment already uses constant-time comparison: signatures.rs:679 (subtle::ConstantTimeEq ct_eq, per Issue #527(e)) and caddy_ask.rs:182/190 (constant_time_eq). voice_webhooks.rs is the outlier. Fix: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq / constant_time_eq on equal-length byte slices.
